purpose: Protriptyline is used to treat depression. It helps improve your mood, energy levels, and overall sense of well-being. It may also be used off-label to help with certain sleep disorders like sleep apnea or narcolepsy.
how_it_works: Your brain uses chemical messengers called serotonin and norepinephrine to help regulate your mood. Protriptyline works by keeping more of these chemicals available in your brain for longer. This helps lift your mood and reduce feelings of depression over time.
common_side_effects: Dry mouth, constipation, blurry vision, dizziness when standing up quickly, drowsiness or trouble sleeping, increased sweating, weight changes, and difficulty urinating. Some people may feel more anxious or restless, especially early on.
warnings: Do not stop taking this medication suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can cause withdrawal symptoms. Protriptyline can cause heart rhythm changes, so tell your doctor if you have any heart problems. It should not be taken with or within 14 days of MAO inhibitor medications, as this can cause a dangerous reaction. This medication may increase thoughts of suicide in young adults, especially in the first few weeks — contact your doctor right away if this happens. Avoid alcohol while taking this medication.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose for adults is 5 to 10 mg taken three or four times a day. Your doctor may slowly increase your dose up to a maximum of 60 mg per day depending on how you respond. Older adults typically start at a lower dose, around 5 mg three times daily, to reduce the risk of side effects.
